title: Build application
description:
Build a **General Help Desk application for enterprises**.

The system should have 3 roles: **Employee, Support Agent, and Admin**.


Core features:

* Employees can create support tickets with **title, description, category, priority, and attachment**.
* Support Agents can **view, assign, update, comment on, and resolve tickets**.
* Ticket status should follow: **Open → Assigned → In Progress → Resolved → Closed**.
* Employees can view their tickets and track status.
* Admin can manage **users, categories, priorities, and tickets**.
* Provide **search, filtering, and dashboards** showing ticket count by status and priority.
* Add proper **mandatory-field validation, error messages, and success messages**.
* Store all ticket changes in an **activity/history log**.
* Create a clean, simple, enterprise-style UI.

Make the application fully functional with working **frontend, backend, database, authentication, validations, and workflows**.

=== CONFIRMED SCOPE AND COMPLEXITY (user-approved — this OVERRIDES any conflicting inference from the brief) ===
* Which functional areas should the Help Desk cover?
  - Include: Ticket Creation & My Tickets; Agent Ticket Desk; Status Workflow & Rules; Admin Setup (Categories & Priorities); Search, Filters & Dashboards; Activity & History Log
  - EXCLUDE (explicitly declined by the user — do NOT specify these): Email Notifications; Response Time Targets (SLA); Knowledge Base & Canned Replies
* How complete should this first version be?
  - Include: Standard
* What should each role see when they log in?
  - Include: Employee: my open tickets; Agent: my queue and workload; Admin: overall ticket health
  - EXCLUDE (explicitly declined by the user — do NOT specify these): Agent performance comparison
* How should a ticket move from Resolved to Closed?
  - Include: Employee confirms
* How should file attachments work on tickets?
  - Include: Multiple files, any time
Write the specification to cover EXACTLY this confirmed scope at the confirmed complexity level: include every confirmed item, honour every added point, and do not add functional areas, activities or enterprise features beyond it.

phases.title: Master & lookup data
phases.rationale: Categories, priorities and the agent roster are referenced by tickets and assignments, so they come first.

phases.title: Core transactions
phases.rationale: Ticket creation, queue handling and assignment depend on the master data built in phase 1.

phases.title: Visuals
phases.rationale: The ticket charts need ticket transaction data to exist first.

phases.title: Dashboards
phases.rationale: The agent and admin dashboards embed visuals and ticket analytics, so they are built last.
